summary: Fairfax tower built by a CCC camp in 1934; register says it was used until about 1978 and taken to Suffolk, VA; now listed as gone.

facts.design: Steel tower with a green roof, per a 1943 Coast & Geodetic Survey description
facts.status_note: Listed as gone. Register says it was used by the FCC until about 1978, then removed to Suffolk, VA; the move is not confirmed by a second source

events.note: Built by CCC Camp P-71 from Camp Recovery, Prince William County
Register removal field reads 1957-1966; the tower dropped off the maps in that span
Used by the FCC until about 1978, then removed to Suffolk, VA, according to Forestry Department interviews
Registered on the Former Fire Lookout Sites Register, March 24, 2020

corrections.proposed: 1957-1966 removal range on the register; relocated to Suffolk, VA about 1978 per Forestry Department interviews
corrections.why: The register records a removal range rather than one year, and the description gives a later move to Suffolk.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The register removal field gives 1957-1966, which matches when the tower dropped off the maps. The description says it was used until about 1978 and then taken to Suffolk, VA. The story reports both; the 1978 move has only the interview account behind it.

notes_for_editor: The Suffolk move rests on one interview account quoted in the register description. The state list shows a standing Dismal Swamp tower in Suffolk, but no source links it to Pender, so the story does not say they are the same. The 30.5 m height comes from the 1933 plan for a 100-foot tower, not a measured figure. The agency text 'now Fifty West Fairfax' is copied as the register gives it; the organization was not identified. No source found for the site today. Research went about two reads over the per-tower budget while checking the Suffolk claim.
